In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have experimentally demonstrated low-loss slow-light propagation in coupled Mie resonator chains at telecom wavelengths.

the proposed coupled silicon nanoparticle waveguides have a potential for future optical interconnect applications, as they provide unique opportunities to enhance and control the light-matter interaction at the nanoscales.

the work presented in this thesis is the first experimental demonstration of a low loss waveguiding device based on coupled Mie resonators and that this new concept may have a significant impact in the future development of integrated nanophotonic devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated a subwavelength silicon waveguide with propagation losses as low as 0.1 dB/mm, and group velocities down to one tenth of the speed of the light.
we demonstrate a sub-wavelength waveguide with low losses and a high level of control over the light propagation.
coupled silicon Mie nanoparticles can be used as an optical waveguide, with low propagation losses and slow light properties, and that this can be achieved in a simple, low cost, and scalable way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
silicon Mie resonances can be used to engineer the dispersion properties of a subwavelength waveguide.
subwavelength waveguide structures based on coupled silicon Mie nanoparticles can be a viable alternative to the traditional waveguides in integrated photonics.
subwavelength silicon nanoparticle waveguides can be used as a new platform for slow light devices and for low loss light guiding.
